description: The golden corpus for the refresh-response.v2 wire contract: a successful refresh whose access token is the EdDSA access-token.v1 JWS. This manifest is the SINGLE inventory: every runner reads THIS file over THESE fixtures (G-70). `reject_by_client` documents are valid against the schema and refused by ParseRefreshResponse: the header and claims rules of access-token.v1 (the same ParseAccessToken), each token's audience (access_token dev-health-api, session_access_token auth-service), its sid against session_id, and expires_in against its exp - iat. Tokens are synthetic, and no fixture stores a compact JWS (as the signed access-token golden corpus does not): each token member is stored as an object {header_json | header_segment, payload_json | payload_segment, signature [, trailing_bits]} and every runner assembles the wire string base64url(header_json) "." base64url(payload_json) "." signature before it validates (a *_segment is used as the segment itself; trailing_bits sets the lowest bit of the last character of the segment it names). Signatures begin EXAMPLE. Go: assembleV2Fixture; ajv: assembleSplitTokens in ci/auth-contracts-ajv/run.mjs.

accept.why: An EdDSA access-token.v1 JWS, 60 minutes, and the 7 day refresh credential.
expires_in is exp - iat of the token, not a constant: ten minutes.

reject.why: The v2 schema accepts only refresh-response.v2; a v1 version string is parsed by the v1 schema.
A lifetime of zero is not a token anyone can use.
Two segments: not a compact JWS.
An empty payload segment: not a compact JWS.
The user object is not part of this contract.
A dot is not in the credential alphabet: a refresh JWT cannot be presented here.
A header segment of nine characters: 4k+1 characters is no base64url.
A padded signature segment: base64url here is unpadded.
The standard-alphabet character + is not in the URL alphabet.
A line break inside a segment; a lenient decoder skips it.
`session_access_token` is required: the session routes accept no other EdDSA token.
Two segments: not a compact JWS.

reject_by_client.why: Header alg HS256: a symmetric algorithm is never this token's (access-token.v1 header).
Header alg none.
Header typ JWT: the HS256 token's type, not at+jwt.
No kid: a verifier could not pick a key.
A jku member moves key selection out of the verifier's hands.
A duplicate member inside the decoded header is refused before any other check.
The token lives 3601 s: over the ceiling although expires_in is in range.
nbf before iat.
expires_in 600 for a token that lives 3600 s.
The token's sid names another session than session_id.
The header decodes to bytes that are not exactly one JSON object.
Schema `integer` admits 3600.0; clients refuse decimal-form tokens.
Duplicate member.
The header segment's last character carries non-zero trailing bits: the same bytes under a second spelling.
The payload segment's last character carries non-zero trailing bits.
The signature segment's last character carries non-zero trailing bits.
access_token carries audience auth-service: the API token is go-api's and query-api's, audience dev-health-api only.
session_access_token carries audience dev-health-api: the session routes accept audience auth-service only.
The session token's sid is not session_id: both tokens are of the one session.
The session token lives 10 minutes while expires_in says 60: both tokens live expires_in.
The session token's header alg is HS256: ParseAccessToken's header rules apply to both tokens.
The session token's payload segment ends in non-zero trailing bits: both tokens are decoded strictly.
